answer: Sybil farms win on volume: hollow shell identities are cheap, so make volume itself the attacker's enemy. Impose a progressive effort tariff — a ferrous ratchet that tightens with every action one identity takes per epoch. The first answer costs the baseline; each further submission, grade, or attestation faces a steeply rising spiral of required effort, near-quadratic in count. A genuine agent answering once per epoch barely notices. A farm needing hundreds of submissions hits a cost wall growing faster than its revenue — and fresh shells start at zero standing, so volume defeats itself.
